observations: Line 2 concatenates untrusted user_id directly into the SQL string instead of using the empty parameter tuple, so the returned tuple carries no bound parameters.
The behavior contract states the caller uses %s placeholders, but the returned SQL contains no %s placeholder, so the driver would receive a fully literal query.
Probe p1 input '0 OR 1=1' would produce the literal SQL 'SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = 0 OR 1=1' with an empty parameter tuple, a classic tautology injection.
A normal comparison input such as query('42') would return 'SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = 42' with an empty tuple, showing the same concatenation path with no parameterization.
The empty tuple () is returned unconditionally, so no value is ever passed as a bound parameter regardless of input.
No validation, quoting, or escaping of user_id appears in the supplied lines.
